1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The present petition has been filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking quashing of the FIR No.
216/2019 under Sections 498A/506/34 IPC registered at Police Station Rajouri Garden on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement.
4. Issue notice.
The learned APP for the State accepts notice.
He submits that since the FIR is an outcome of a matrimonial dispute and the parties have arrived at a settlement, the State has no objection in case the FIR in This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text: He submits that the learned Trial Court has also taken cognizance against the present petitioners vide order dated 16.12.2021.

He further submits that notwithstanding the taking of cognizance by the learned Trial Court only against the present petitioners, Amandeep Singh whose name is mentioned in column 12 of the charge sheet is present in Court and three other persons namely Ravinder Kaur, Darshan Kaur Gujral and Jasmeet Kaur whose names are also mentioned in column 12 of the charge sheet have joined through VC.
The respondent no.2 is also present in court.
8. The parties who are present in court, as well as, those who have joined through VC have been identified by their respective counsels and by the SI Naveen (I.O), PS Rajouri Garden.
9. The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the parties was solemnised on 09.02.2018 as per Sikh Rites and Customs.

Out of the said wedlock, one girl child namely Satwinder Kaur @ Devanshi was born who is presently in the care and custody of the respondent no.2.
10.
On account of temperamental issues certain disputes arose between the parties and they started living separately w.e.f. 09.05.2018 from each other.
The dispute between the parties also led to the registration of present FIR.

During the pendency of the proceedings, the parties have arrived at a settlement, terms whereof were reduced in writing in the form of "Memorandum of Settlement for marriage divorce" dated 10.10.2022, which is annexed as Annexure A-3 to the present petition.
12. In terms of the said settlement, the parties decided to dissolve their marriage by filing a petition seeking mutual divorce under Sections 13B(1) and 13B(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

Accordingly,
the parties have obtained a decree of divorce dated 24.05.2023, which is annexed as Annexure A-5 (page 86 of the paper book) to the present petition.

13. It is also a term of the settlement between the parties that the petitioner no.1 shall pay a total sum of Rs.8.5 lacs to the respondent no.2 towards full and final settlement of all her claims on account of maintenance (past, present and future), permanent alimony, stree dhan and dowry articles.

Out of the said amount, a sum of Rs.7 lacs has already been paid by the petitioner no.1 to the respondent no.2 in the manner as mentioned in MoU/Settlement dated 10.10.2022, the receipt of which respondent no.2 acknowledges.

The remaining amount of Rs.1.5 lacs has been paid to the respondent no.2 today in the court by way of Demand Draft bearing no.127520 dated 11.09.2023 issued by the Union Bank of India, Vikaspuri, New Delhi in favour of Inderpreet Kaur.
14. The respondent no.2 who is present in court
acknowledges having receipt the entire settlement amount of Rs. 8.5 lacs.
